recomputed: I matched SHA-256 and byte count for all 11 SOURCES.tsv entries. Fresh NCBI downloads of the DE CSV, family SOFT and Salmon matrix also matched byte for byte. All three gzip files decompressed through EOF. I parsed the 24,405-row DE export, all 16 GEO sample records and all 45,706 matrix rows and 16 count columns. The six JSON files contain the stated bibliographic records or search responses. Poppler extracted both pages of the German MedWiss news item. The publisher text file contains indexed article excerpts. I checked all seven comparison input hashes, the registry, five authored ledgers, current generated comparison, R model provenance and v2 criteria. The four KO IP pools are GSM8858615–GSM8858618 and the four control IP pools are GSM8858623–GSM8858626. Each pool contains four mice. Both effect columns are KO minus control within IP. The author table contains 13,989 finite genotype effect/FDR pairs and 10,416 missing pairs, with no raw P column. All 16,832 registered effects and FDRs are finite. The independent one-to-one join gives 13,946 pairs, covering 82.854087% of registered effects and 99.692616% of finite author effects. Even a perfect join covers at most 83.109553% of the registered table. Unpaired registered counts are 2,621 with missing author genotype estimates, 221 without an author row and 44 multi-ID aggregates. Pearson is 0.99979948, Spearman 0.99977600 and 13,545/13,946 nonzero signs agree (97.124624%). Median absolute log2FC difference is 0.01147748, RMS difference 0.01229714 and registered-to-author RMS ratio 1.00164346. At FDR < 0.05, whole-table counts are 1,052 author and 89 registered. Paired counts are 1,049 author, 84 registered and 84 shared (Jaccard 0.08007626). Three author and five registered calls lie outside the one-to-one comparison. Four of the five registered calls have missing author FDR and one is an aggregate. The source-ID join resolves 864 differing names. The built-in literal-symbol join gives 13,116 pairs (77.923004%), 993/77/77 paired calls, five conflicting IDs and 31 aggregates. Both versions of the paper’s inequalities select identical IDs. They give 2,048 WT and 1,502 KO enrichments, 1,202 in both, 2,348 distinct enriched IDs, 1,052 genotype DE and 236 joint calls. Of these 2,348, 2,197 have both volcano coordinates. The GEO rule gives 1,309 WT and 898 KO enrichments, 701 in both, 1,506 distinct enriched, 365 genotype DE and 69 joint calls. All 69 occur in the paper-rule 236. I matched every reconstructed selection.tsv identifier, label and membership flag. Selection used source-defined cutoffs on the full deposit. The primary matching rule uses only feature identity. Both numerical agreement routes pass, but registered coverage falls below 90%. The correction retains closure compared, full_results as the input scope, limited assessment and an empty sign-off list.
problems: The proposed promotion to validated_with_notes and method_differences would clear an observed discrepancy. The paper calls 3,550 genes enriched in either genotype. That number equals the sum of the two arm counts, which includes 1,202 IDs twice. Only 2,348 distinct IDs meet the rule, and 2,197 have finite genotype statistics for Figure 4B. The authors’ reason for reporting 3,550 and the membership of their original plot remain unknown. The corrected review retains review_required and unresolved while recording the completed comparison.

The manual summary implied that the authors’ 236-gene membership had been verified. The reported count is reproducible and the inferred list matches selection.tsv. There is no independent author list in the reviewed material against which to verify all 236 identities.

The proposed publisher_full_text override would display ‘Publisher full text accessed’. The retained file is an index capture. Independent checks recovered the relevant indexed sections, while direct article and PDF routes returned HTTP 403. The corrected manual record omits the optional override so its replacement uses the existing source-inventory access value. The review flags document exactly which publisher passages were available.

The cohort assessment omitted a scope discrepancy with the registry. GEO and the paper describe pooled hypothalamic dissections. Pool labels support the eight-library match, while individual animal IDs and an ARC-only dissection are undocumented. The corrected proposal also identifies the registry’s citation discrepancy with PMID 40273910.
